prose: Part One of Ed Zitron's premium 'Hater's Guide to Circular Financing' opens with a satirical set piece: an NVIDIA company meeting where Jensen Huang leads the crowd in celebrating that the AI labs can't actually afford his GPUs - 'Clammy Sammy and Wario Amodei's' labs lose money, while 'big strong men like Satya Nadella' beg for Vera Rubin shipments. The cartoon version makes the essay's point physical: everyone's money is everyone else's revenue.

Beneath the theater, the piece sets up the series' argument about the AI build-out's circular money flows - NVIDIA investing in the customers who buy its chips with cloud intermediaries in between - and Huang's trillion-dollar Grace Blackwell/Vera Rubin shipment claims as the hype layer on top. (Premium post; summary based on the freely available opening.)
highlights: Opens with a satirical NVIDIA meeting mocking the AI labs' inability to pay for GPUs
Huang caricatured boasting of a trillion dollars of Grace Blackwell/Vera Rubin shipments by end of 2027
The skit dramatizes circular financing: NVIDIA's investors, customers and clouds are the same money
